newsitem.title: USA: House ethics panel approves Gingrich loan from Dole.
newsitem.headline: House ethics panel approves Gingrich loan from Dole.

text.p: The House ethics committee Thursday approved a loan of up $150,000 loan from Bob Dole to House Speaker Newt Gingrich to help Gingrich pay a $300,000 ethics penalty.
The speaker's office also announced that Gingrich had made an initial payment of $50,000 from his own funds.
Under the plan approved by the ethics panel, Gingrich is scheduled to make additional $50,000 payments on June 1 and Nov. 30, 1998. A $150,000 payment would be due on Jan. 2, 1999.

Gingrich would borrow up to $150,000 from former Republican presidential nominee Dole to make the final payment. As collateral, the speaker pledged his home in Georgia and proceeds from a second book to be published by Harper Collins Publishing Inc. under an existing contract.
The five-year loan from Dole would carry a 10 percent interest rate. Gingrich would have to start paying off the loan Jan. 2, 2000.
In a letter to Gingrich, ethics committee officials said the terms of the loan were "commercially reasonable and in conformance with House rules and standards."
